name: Sunn O)))
label: Southern Lord
lede: Two Seattle guitarists worship Earth with a stack of Sunn amps, then spend twenty-five years turning that hum into cathedral sets, Scott Walker sessions and a fog-drowned ritual.

eras.title: Two guitarists, one worshipped band
eras.text: Stephen O'Malley and Greg Anderson leave Burning Witch behind and build a tribute to Earth out of Sunn amplifiers. The first records are drones with a debt to Dylan Carlson and a stubborn sense of humor.

years.h: Greg Anderson starts Southern Lord to control his own records
years.p: Anderson founds Southern Lord in April 1998, first putting out Thorr's Hammer and Burning Witch. It becomes Sunn O)))'s long-term home.

years.h: A band named after an amp, and a nod to Earth
years.p: Sunn O))) forms in Seattle in 1998 and is named for the Sunn amplifier brand. O'Malley has said the name also plays on [[Earth|60dd41cf-8f9d-46d8-bc19-dc7e5acb24c8]].
years.xp:
Both men came out of [[Burning Witch|e5d4491d-1496-4efa-a5b9-e7be001b9f6a]] (O'Malley) and [[Goatsnake|ae720a02-629e-4e9b-98e7-d1f637bd5a49]] (Anderson). They had watched Earth in the 1990s and worn out its records, and Sunn O))) began as a tribute to that band, whose amp of choice was Sunn.

Wikipedia notes the pair briefly played as Mars before settling on the name, and later moved to Los Angeles.

years.h: The Grimmrobe Demos: two guitars, no polish
years.p: The first Sunn O))) recordings surface as The Grimmrobe Demos on Hydra Head Records. They show the band's whole plan: one chord, huge amps, long silence.

years.h: ØØ Void arrives on Hydra Head
years.p: Recorded on 2-inch tape at Grandmaster Studios in Hollywood with producer Scott Reeder. It covers the Melvins' "Rabbits' Revenge" and is issued by Hydra Head in North America and Rise Above in Europe.
years.xp: Pitchfork later gave it 7.5 out of 10. Southern Lord reissued it in 2011 in a single-disc edition with new artwork; a 2008 Japanese edition had added a collaboration with Nurse with Wound.

years.cap: Sunn amps between band and crowd
q: We've got to come up with something where we feel comfortable.
years.h: A cold London crowd, and a wall of amps in front of the band
years.p: On an early UK tour with Goatsnake and Orange Goblin, Anderson says audiences were unreceptive. At The Underworld in London the band stacked amps between themselves and the room.
years.xp: Anderson told The Quietus that the reaction pushed them toward something they were comfortable doing on stage. That became robes, fog and anonymity rather than rock-band posing.

eras.title: Robes, fog and a Mayhem singer
eras.text: Southern Lord takes over as the band's label, and Attila Csihar turns a two-man drone into a ritual. White1 and White2 open the doors, then Black One turns black metal loose in the room.

years.h: Flight of the Behemoth, the first on Southern Lord
years.p: The band's second album lands on Anderson's own label. From here on Southern Lord is home for almost every Sunn O))) release.

years.cap: Attila Csihar on stage with Sunn O)))
years.h: Attila Csihar's first show, in Linz, Austria
years.p: The [[Mayhem|c5f9e699-7b0d-4030-86dd-7acc8250d147]] vocalist joins Sunn O))) live for the first time on March 24, 2003 at Stadtwerkstatt in Linz. He has since done hundreds of shows with them.
years.xp: Csihar had sung on Mayhem's De Mysteriis Dom Sathanas (1994) after the death of vocalist Dead. He first recorded with Sunn O))) in 2004, singing in Sanskrit on two White2 tracks.

years.h: White1: Julian Cope recites on "My Wall"
years.p: Julian Cope reads poetry on "My Wall"; Runhild Gammelsæter of Thorr's Hammer opens "The Gates of Ballard" in Norwegian. Joe Preston plays guitar, bass and electronics.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports Q magazine's loud issue ranked White1 18th loudest album ever, between Back in Black and Are You Experienced.

years.h: White2 puts Attila Csihar on record
years.p: Csihar sings in Sanskrit on "Decay2 [Nihil's Maw]" and "Decay (The Symptoms of Kali Yuga)", his first studio work with the band.

years.h: Black One: black metal voices in drone
years.p: The band's fifth album brings black metal figures into their world, including Wrest of Leviathan and Malefic of Xasthur.

years.h: Boris and Sunn O))) make Altar
years.p: The Japanese band Boris and Sunn O))) release the collaboration Altar on Halloween 2006 through Southern Lord, with guests including Jesse Sykes.
years.xp: Guests included Joe Preston and Jesse Sykes, and Kim Thayil of Soundgarden.

eras.title: A cathedral and a chamber orchestra
eras.text: Sunn O))) stops being a drone band and becomes a composing one. A live set in a Norwegian cathedral leads into Monoliths & Dimensions, their most ambitious record.

years.h: Bergen Cathedral, Borealis Festival: Dømkirke
years.p: The band play a live set inside Bergen Cathedral in Norway on March 18, 2007, with Attila Csihar, Steve Moore and Lasse Marhaug. It comes out on vinyl in 2008.

years.h: Monoliths & Dimensions: horns, harp, a women's choir
years.p: Two years in the making, with Eyvind Kang on viola and arrangements, trombonists Julian Priester and Stuart Dempster, Dylan Carlson and Oren Ambarchi. It closes on "Alice", a tribute to Alice Coltrane.
years.xp: Metacritic scores it 88. O'Malley called the album the most musical and heaviest thing they had done, per Wikipedia. They had also invited Scott Walker to sing on it; he declined for scheduling reasons.

years.h: Scott Walker says no, then calls back five years later
years.p: Scott Walker turned down a slot on Monoliths & Dimensions in 2009. He was later the one who came to them.
years.xp: Walker told an interviewer about the space the drones gave him between phrases. That call leads to Soused, in 2014.

eras.title: Ulver, Scott Walker and Kannon
eras.text: The band lets outsiders in: Norwegian art-rockers Ulver, then Scott Walker himself, and the 33-minute Kannon.

years.h: Terrestrials with Ulver
years.p: Sunn O))) and the Norwegian group Ulver put out a collaborative album on Southern Lord.

years.h: Sunn O))) haul their whole stage rig to London for Scott Walker
years.p: For Soused on 4AD, they brought their entire amp collection to Walker's London studio and followed his wordless synth demos.
years.xp: Walker sent O'Malley and Anderson synthesizer demos outlining the parts they should play. Producer credits went to Walker and Peter Walsh. Metacritic scores it 83.

years.h: Kannon: three long drones in 33 minutes
years.p: Produced by O'Malley, Anderson and Randall Dunn, with Attila Csihar's vocals. Guests include Oren Ambarchi, Steve Moore and Brad Mowen on bass drum.

eras.title: Steve Albini and a father's mood
eras.text: The band cuts a record fully analog in Chicago, then a second one straight after.

q: Having children and being a father has really changed me.
years.h: Steve Albini records Life Metal in two weeks
years.p: Recorded in July 2018 at Electrical Audio, it's their first fully analog record, with Hildur Guðnadóttir on cello and Anthony Pateras on pipe organ.
years.xp: The title began as a joke against death metal. Anderson said becoming a father changed how he thought about writing music. Metacritic scores it 85.

years.h: Pyroclasts follows six months after Life Metal
years.p: A companion record released on Southern Lord, in the same year as Life Metal.

eras.title: Sub Pop and back to a duo
eras.text: After decades at Southern Lord, Sunn O))) signs with Sub Pop and records their tenth album as just Anderson and O'Malley.

years.h: Two men, no guests, in Woodinville
years.p: Sunn O))) record their tenth album at Bear Creek Studios in Woodinville, Washington, co-produced with Brad Wood. O'Malley and Anderson play everything themselves.

years.h: Sunn O))) sign to Sub Pop
years.p: Wikipedia dates the Sub Pop signing to October 14, 2025, the same day as the EP Eternity's Pillars.

years.h: Self-titled tenth album, their first on Sub Pop
years.p: It arrives April 3, 2026, with North American headlining dates through April and May.
